summary: retracfix postinstall auto-executes bundled Windows.NET RAT/infostealer
details: Package ships a Windows-only.NET executable at bin/ezfn.exe and a postinstall.js launcher that locates the first.exe under bin/ and runs it via spawnSync with the installer's environment on every `npm install` (gated to os:[win32]). The bundled binary's.NET metadata contains the capability set of a commodity RAT/stealer: socket C2 (ClientSocket, ConnectServer, ActivatePong), Telegram Bot API exfiltration (SendBot, ChatID), Windows Defender exclusion setup (Antivirus, Exclusion), self-propagation (Spread), remote payload download (WebClient/DownloadString), host reconnaissance (get_UserName, get_MachineName, get_OSFullName, get_TotalPhysicalMemory, ManagementObjectSearcher), and registry access plus symmetric decryption routines (RegistryKey/CurrentUser, System.Security.Cryptography.CreateDecryptor) consistent with stored-credential extraction. The package has an empty description, ships no source or README, and its only install-time effect is executing this opaque binary — a total mismatch between advertised purpose and shipped contents. Installing on Windows hands the host to a remote operator and exfiltrates identity and credential-shaped data to an attacker-controlled Telegram channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
